_comment: Fragment 55 — D-101: D-100 propagated to its executors, response separated from closure, Q11's shape reaches the Build Spec. Merged 2026-08-24.

nodes.label: B-011 — A Ruling the Executing Agent Cannot See Has Not Been Propagated
nodes.description: The operating-model ruling withdrew strict phase serialization and redefined what a handoff means, then recorded the Build Spec and all three agent rule files as unaffected. Those files still said sequentially, one at a time, in a fixed phase order, with one lane now and one lane next.
nodes.rationale: The register winning on precedence is the wrong comfort: the build lane's own instructions say governance reaches it as a flag and that it is not expected to read the register. Following the rule file waits for a gate that no longer exists; following the register resumes. Either action violates an operative instruction, which makes this a deterministic conflict rather than a risk.

nodes.label: D-101 — The Model Propagated and Closure Separated From Response
nodes.description: Exactly one lane is Active and the others are Eligible rather than queued. Four states replace the ambiguous Open. Five closure fields and a derived matrix separate a reply from a fix.
nodes.rationale: The one-desktop, one-agent-at-a-time constraint is physical and unchanged. What the earlier ruling removed was the queue, not the serialization, and saying so explicitly is what the build lane asked for.

nodes.label: The Rule Files No Longer Carry Lane State
nodes.description: The build lane asked for a check that fails when the register and a rule file disagree about which lane is current. Instead the rule files stopped carrying lane state at all: they define the vocabulary and point at the phase register.
nodes.rationale: Removing a duplicate is stronger than checking it, because there is then nothing to disagree with. A status copied into a rule file is the drift mechanism this register has recorded repeatedly.

nodes.label: Stop-and-Wait Was a Rule About One Entry, Generalised
nodes.description: One decision said a lane needing a dependency stops and waits; a later one said feedback enters the backlog while work continues. Both are right about different entries. A blocking entry stops that item; a non-blocking one goes to the top of the backlog.
nodes.rationale: The earlier wording took a blocking dependency and made it a rule about every handoff. Resolving it per entry keeps both statements true instead of choosing between them.

nodes.label: Check 13 — Silent Until Closure Is Claimed
nodes.description: Derives the closure matrix from the handoff entries' own fields and reports it on every run. It gates only when the phase register marks a phase closed, and then fails on any entry that is merely Open or Answered.
nodes.rationale: A full backlog during a sprint is healthy and a check that fired on it would be ignored within a week. An unverified blocker at a Judge boundary is a different thing. No second backlog file exists, because a file listing the entries would restate them and restatements drift.

nodes.label: Three Positional-Parsing Defects, Then the Approach Changed
nodes.description: A check dropped compound rows; a detector matched a different three-column table and read its last column as the closed cell; then the register gained a lane column and every fixed index shifted. Both detectors now read the register by column name from its header row.
nodes.rationale: A header-driven parser cannot be broken by adding a column. Three instances is where the approach changes rather than the pattern, and the second and third were introduced by the lane fixing the first.

nodes.label: B-012 — A Decision That Does Not Reach the Tier an Author Reads
nodes.description: The register and the product requirements row recorded the three-value shape while the Build Spec still called the question deferred and named the boolean fallback. The same paragraph had already been reported once.
nodes.rationale: A future migration author reads the Build Spec. Two tiers pointing at incompatible stored shapes means one of them produces a schema that cannot compute its declared guardrail from its declared data source.

nodes.label: The Provisional Markers Are Deliberately Not Cleared
nodes.description: The shape is decided and the name is not. The six provisional markers depend on the naming half, so clearing them would treat a half-answered question as closed. The earlier deferral is reconciled: it was of the naming half only.
nodes.rationale: Clearing a marker because a related question was answered is the conflation the entry reports. Recording the two halves separately is what lets the shape bind while the name stays open.
